title: 6:39AM VIOLENT MORNING DECLARATIONS
text: Let me ask you something. When was the last time your prayer shook a room? Not a room in a building, a room in the spirit. When was the last time you prayed and something moved? Not [music] eventually, not later that week, immediately. When was the last time you prayed and the atmosphere shifted so fast that everyone present felt it? If your honest answer is I cannot remember, then today is the day everything changes because there is a prayer recorded in the book of Acts. A prayer so specific, so dangerous, so theologically loaded that when it was prayed, the building they were sitting in shook, the ground moved, [music] the Holy Ghost fell, and a company of believers who had just been threatened by the most powerful authorities of their age walked out of that room speaking with a boldness that turned their world upside down. That prayer is in Acts chapter 4:29, and by the time we finish today, you will not just know it, you will pray it, you will pray it the way they prayed it >> [music] >> with the weight, with the theology, with the fire, and you will watch what happens. But first right now, before the teaching begins, [music] share this word. Do not wait. There is a believer in your network who has gone silent. They used to pray, they used to speak with fire, but something happened, a threat, a disappointment, a prolonged unanswered season, and the boldness left. They are still saved, they are still in church, but the voice has been reduced to a whisper, and this word is the restoration of that voice. Share it now as an act of intercession. Send the fire to the person who needs it most. Then come back because what God is about to release in this room will not leave you the same. Open your Bible to Acts chapter 4. I need to give you context because the prayer of Acts 4:29 cannot be understood without understanding the moment it was prayed in. Peter and John had just healed a lame man at the gate called Beautiful. Acts chapter 3. A man who had never walked in his life, lame from his mother's womb, more than 40 years old. And at the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, he leaped to his feet and walked. >> [music] >> The city was shaken. The temple was disrupted. And the Sanhedrin, the highest religious and political authority in the land, called Peter and John before them. They interrogated them. They threatened them. They commanded them to speak no more in the name of Jesus. Acts 4:18. And they called them and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus. This is a governmental order. This is the highest authority in the land saying, "Be silent." >> [music] >> Stop the name. Stop the miracles. Stop the movement or face the consequences. And what did Peter and John do? They went back to their own company and they reported everything that had been said to them. Acts 4:24. And when they heard that, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord. One accord. [music] They did not scatter in fear. They did not hold a crisis meeting to discuss their options. They did not negotiate with the threat. They gathered. They unified. And they lifted up their voice to God. Now, listen to how they prayed. Because this is the part that nobody talks about. They did not pray, "Lord, [music] protect us from the Sanhedrin." They did not pray, "Lord, let the threat stop." They did not pray, "Lord, make this easier for us." Acts 4:24 through 28. They prayed a theology. They reminded God of who he is. They said, "Lord, thou art God, which has made heaven and earth and the sea and all that in them is." They declared his sovereignty over creation before they made a single request. They recall scripture Psalm 2 about the kings of the earth taking counsel against the Lord. They connected their present persecution to a prophetic pattern. They said Herod and Pilate, the Gentiles and the people of Israel did whatsoever thy hand and thy counsel determined before to be done. Did you hear that? They said everything that happened to Jesus, [music] the crucifixion, the rejection, the suffering was already in the counsel of God. It was not a surprise to heaven and neither is what you are going through. There are dimensions to this that the average believer has never assessed. Most believers pray from panic. The early church prayed from theology. There is a difference. When you pray from panic, you are asking God to catch up with your situation. When you pray from theology, you are reminding yourself that God was already there. The theology does not change God's knowledge of the situation. It changes your posture in the situation. It moves you from victim to victor, from the threatened to the sent. Now verse 29. Here it is, the prayer that shook the building. And now Lord behold their threatenings and grant onto thy servants that with all boldness they may speak thy word. Read it again. Let it sit. The Sanhedrin just threatened them with everything they had. The most powerful human authorities in their world just commanded them to be silent and [music] their prayer, their response, their petition to heaven was not Lord destroy our enemies, was not Lord avenge us, was not Lord grant us safety, protection, comfort, relief. It was Lord grant us boldness. This is the most counterintuitive prayer in all of scripture. The natural response to threat is to ask for protection. The apostolic response to threat is to ask for boldness. Hear me, this is not theology. This is encounter. The early church understood something that most of the modern church has forgotten. The assignment does not stop because the opposition increases. The mandate does not shrink because the threats get louder. If anything, when the enemy intensifies the pressure, it is a signal that the assignment is working. It is evidence that what you are carrying is threatening the kingdom of darkness, and the answer to that signal is not retreat. It is advance. The spirit of God is saying something right now. He's saying some of you have retreated. The pressure came and the voice got smaller. The opposition mounted and the steps got shorter. The threats arrived and the boldness was quietly put away like a garment you no longer felt you had the right to wear. But that garment was not taken from you. You set it down. And today God is saying pick it back up. Now three words in this prayer. Three words that unlock the entire weight of Acts 4:29. Behold, grant boldness. Behold, they said Lord behold their threatenings. Not Lord, ignore their threatenings. Not Lord, [music] pretend the threats are not real. Behold them. Look at them. Examine them. Let your eyes fall upon what has been said against us. This is the prayer of those who have nothing to hide from God. They are bringing the threat into the open before heaven. They are not minimizing it. They are not exaggerating it. They are presenting it to the one whose gaze changes everything it falls upon. Psalm 33:2-18, behold the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him. When the eye of the Lord beholds your enemy, your enemy is exposed. When the eye of the Lord beholds the threat, the threat is measured against omnipotence, [music] and nothing survives that measurement unchanged. I grant they ask God to grant boldness, not to manufacture it themselves, not to summon it from their own reserves. Grant from you, a gift, a bestowal, a divine endowment. This is the wisdom of the apostolic church. They knew that the boldness required for the assignment was not natural boldness. Natural boldness can be silenced by a large enough threat. Natural boldness has limits, but granted boldness, boldness that comes from the throne of God, that boldness does not compute the size of the threat. >> [music] >> It only knows the size of the one who sent it. Acts 4:31, and when they had prayed, [music and singing] the place was shaken where they were assembled together, and they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they speak the word of God with boldness. >> [music] >> God answered the prayer, not with silence, not gradually, immediately, physically, atmospherically, the place was shaken. The building moved. The physical structure of the room they were praying in responded to the prayer. God shook the building. And [music] listen, he did not shake the building of the Sanhedrin. He shook the building of the believers. He started [music] with the room where the prayer was. He started with the company that prayed. He shook them first, and then he sent them out to shake everything else. I need you to stay with me, because this sequence is everything. [music] The shaking starts in the prayer room. The shaking starts in the place of intercession. The shaking starts in the [music and singing] gathered, unified, boldness-seeking company of believers, and from that shaken room, they go out, and [music] what they carry shakes everywhere they put their feet. Boldness. The Greek word is parresia. >> [music] >> It means freedom of speech, unreservedness, confidence, openness. But, in the first-century context, it had a specific technical meaning. Parresia was the right of a free citizen to speak in the public assembly without fear. It was the legal right to stand in the public square and say what you believed. The early church was using a citizenship term. They were saying, "Lord, grant us the parresia of heaven citizens to speak in its public square. We are not asking for permission from Rome. We are not asking for clearance from the Sanhedrin. We are invoking our citizenship in a kingdom that supersedes every earthly authority." Philippians chapter 3, verse 20, "For our conversation is in heaven." The word conversation there is politeuma, citizenship. Our citizenship is in heaven, and the rights that come with that citizenship cannot be revoked by any earthly power. Thus saith the spirit of God. >> [music] >> The threats against you do not have authority over a citizen of heaven. The intimidation of the enemy does not have jurisdiction over a child of God. The Sanhedrin of your life, whatever form it has taken, your boss who told you to be silent about your faith, the system that told you your calling is not valid, the principality that has been suppressing your voice for years, they do not have authority over parresia, they do not have authority over the boldness that comes from the throne of God. Now, verses 29 through 30, because there is something in verse 30 that most people miss. "And now, Lord, behold their threatenings, and grant unto thy servants that with all boldness they may speak thy word, by stretching forth thine hand [clears throat] to heal, and that signs and wonders may be done by the name of thy holy child Jesus. >> [music] >> They prayed for boldness, and then they said by stretching forth thine hand to heal, by signs and wonders done in the name of Jesus. The boldness they were asking for was not the boldness to give opinions. It was not the boldness to be controversial. It was not the boldness to offend people. >> [music] >> It was the boldness to speak a word that God would confirm with miracles. They were asking for the boldness of demonstration, the boldness that opens a mouth and God stretches forth his hand. The boldness that speaks a word and the deaf ear opens. The boldness that declares healing and the body responds. The boldness that prophesies and [music] the thing happens. Mark chapter 16 verse 20, "And they went forth and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word with signs following." The Lord working with them, not ahead of them without them, not behind them as an afterthought. With them, in partnership, in tandem. The human opens the mouth, the divine stretches the hand. The human speaks the word, the divine confirms it with power. This is the prayer [music] of Acts 4:29. Not just make me brave enough my mouth, but when I open my mouth, Lord, stretch your hand. Let what I speak be confirmed by what you do. Let the word carry the weight of the one who sent it. >> [music] >> I decree and declare over every life under the sound of this voice, the hand of God is about to stretch alongside your voice. When you speak, he will confirm. When you declare, he will demonstrate. When you open your mouth in boldness, heaven will back you. >> [music] >> Now we pray and I want you to understand exactly what we are doing. We are praying the prayer of Acts 4:29. We are praying it in the same spirit the early church prayed it with theology first then petition. With the acknowledgement of who God is before the acknowledgement of what we need. We are going to behold the threats before God. We are going to ask for granted boldness and we are going to ask him to stretch forth his hand >> [music] >> and then we are going to watch what happens. Stand. If you are in the room, lift your voice. This is not the kind of prayer that is prayed quietly. The early church lifted up their voice plural, unified, unashamed. Lift your voice now. Lord, thou art God. Thou art God which has made heaven and earth and the sea and all that in them is. >> [music] >> You are not a regional deity. You are not a cultural concept. You are the creator, the sovereign, the one whose voice formed galaxies. And the same voice that said let there be light is the voice that is hearing this prayer right now. We acknowledge you. We establish your sovereignty over this situation before we present the situation. Nothing that has come against us is outside your knowledge. Psalm 121:2-4, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep. And now Lord, behold their threatenings. We bring the threats before you now. Every threat that has been made against the lives connected to this prayer, not metaphorically, literally. The threat of financial ruin, Lord, behold it. When the eye of the Lord falls on what the enemy has assembled, the assembly begins to fall apart. The plans begin to unravel. The weapons begin to fail.
